literal: Those who stood in the path of virtuous conduct free from falsehood of the one who extinguished the five gateways of the senses, will live long.
translation: Those who stand steadfast in the true path of virtuous conduct, shown by the One who subdued the five senses, will live forever.
modern: ஐந்து புலன்களாகிய வாயில்களை அடக்கிய இறைவனுடைய, பொய் இல்லாத ஒழுக்க நெறியில் நிலைத்து நிற்பவர்கள், நெடுங்காலம் வாழ்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet describes the reward of following the path of virtue shown by the Divine. The Divine is characterized as 'aintavittāṉ', the one who has completely subdued the five sensory organs, representing ultimate self-control. The path of conduct ('oḻukka neṟi') shown by such a being is 'poytīr'—entirely free from falsehood and illusion. Those who firmly abide ('niṉṟār') by this true path of virtue will enjoy an enduring, spiritually fulfilling life ('nīṭu vāḻvār').
